metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent started on macys.com homepage but got Access Denied on all macys.com subdirectory pages. Task limit reached after 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Agent demonstrated clicking UI elements, keyboard shortcuts, and interacting with Chrome. The Macy's homepage was loaded and accessible at task start.
metadata.failure_analysis: Original task failed because macys.com subdirectory navigation returned Access Denied. The homepage itself was always accessible.
metadata.task_rationale: Uses the accessible macys.com homepage (already open in initial state) to test bookmark addition — a demonstrated Chrome UI interaction capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires bookmarking the Macy's homepage. Custom metric checks that the bookmarks bar contains a URL matching 'macys.com'. Initial state starts with macys.com open so the agent just needs to add a bookmark. [Fixed: replaced inner def _search_node with iterative stack-based traversal to eliminate unnamed helper function that failed MD5 naming validation]
fix_history: Fix 1: Replaced recursive inner function _search_node with iterative stack-based DFS to satisfy check_{semantic}__{32-char-md5} naming rule — inner def caused validator to flag _search_node as a metric missing an MD5 suffix

validation.fix_applied: Replaced inner def _search_node with iterative stack traversal; no inner function definitions remain in metrics/macys_bookmark.py
llm_judge_reasons: The get_bookmarks getter correctly reads Chrome's Bookmarks JSON file and returns data.get('roots', {}), which contains the 'bookmark_bar' key used by the metric.
The metric restricts its DFS search to the 'bookmark_bar' node only, directly matching the instruction requirement of adding to the bookmarks bar (not other folders).
URL matching uses 'macys.com' in url, which correctly matches 'https://www.macys.com/' and any macys.com subdomain.
The iterative DFS correctly traverses Chrome's nested bookmark structure (folders have 'children' lists, leaves have 'url' fields).
The initial state (fresh chrome snapshot with macys.com open but not bookmarked) should not pass the check — negative control resistance is sound.
The evaluator correctly verifies all requirements of the instruction: that the Macy's homepage URL is present specifically in the bookmarks bar.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The fallback key 'Bookmarks bar' in result.get('bookmark_bar', result.get('Bookmarks bar', {})) is not a real Chrome JSON key (actual key is 'bookmark_bar'), but this is a minor redundancy — the primary key works correctly.
